title_en: 'This Is Akin to a Moon Landing' - How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond
summary_en: GTA 6 is finally almost here, and the world's biggest content creators are trying to figure out how to handle this behemoth.
body_en:
GTA 6 is finally upon us and it’s expected to be a cultural juggernaut that overshadows everything in its path. This includes other game releases, movies, and even upcoming holidays, such as Thanksgiving in the United States. Economists estimate a $1 billion loss in productivity during the game’s launch weekend , as millions of people are expected to take time off work to play Rockstar’s highly anticipated game. All in all, it's hard to overstate the impact its arrival will have.
“To me, every GTA feels like a generational moon landing,” said Mary Kish, the Head of Community Marketing at Twitch. “It's so big, and it's so prolific, and it changes culture and my life to such a large extent that it can feel overwhelming.”
However, there is one group of people that are going to be working non-stop for the next month: content creators. Typically, content creators are given games earlier so they can make all kinds of videos about the game. I spoke with some of the top YouTubers and streamers in the world, including in the GTA space, and none of them have the game. That even goes for a popular GTA YouTuber known as TGG, who has 2.32 million subscribers. He was exclusively invited to Rockstar North over the summer to be one of the only people to see GTA 6 before its release and became a primary source for anyone seeking information about the elusive game. And yet, Rockstar withheld the full game even from him.
This isn’t common for a major AAA video game. It shows the lengths Rockstar is going to to preserve and protect its blockbuster, which has been guarded with a veil of secrecy for most of the last decade. Rockstar has been very calculated with how and when it chooses to show what it has been working on. The company has subtly sprinkled short gameplay clips and teasers in the final days before release , but that’s about it. There aren’t any YouTubers who have weeks of uploads banked and ready to go, meaning almost everyone is going into this game completely blind and on the same level playing field.
That has presented a unique situation for a lot of these creators. Everyone I spoke with made it clear that this is a game they are genuinely excited for. Although they have a job to do, they have all waited years for this moment as a fan. Despite the pressure to make content, they all told me they plan to take their time with the game so they can savor it, with some of them estimating that it may take over 100 hours before they actually roll credits on it.
A lot of preparation is going into this launch weekend. Some creators are hiring extra help in the form of additional writers and editors, while others are planning on making a spectacle out of things. Numerous streamers have rented mansions in Miami to not only do massive, extravagant streams, but also celebrate the launch with others in person.
Introducing the Midnight Launch, in celebration of the release of GTA VI
Exclusive prizes, game giveaways, merch, and more
In Miami, November 18th-19th. Presented by HyperX https://t.co/fYk4LqHSZZ
Gaming peripheral company HyperX is teaming up with Gaming World Media to host a flashy in-person midnight launch event in Miami with fans and streamers. This is not something being done in partnership with Rockstar. It’s just a group of creators and a gaming hardware company putting their money together to do something special. According to GMW co-founder Jake Lucky, the goal is to recapture the magic of a shared in-person gaming experience.
“Essentially we are throwing a party for people who are just as excited for GTA as we are,” said GWM co-founder Jake Lucky in a statement to IGN. “[We are giving] attendees not only a chance to play, but also [a chance to] win their own copy, exclusive merch, and even GTA inspired collectibles to remember the event by. I just really think it’s important to bring back the human aspect of game launches that we have lost in modern times”
This is a big moment for Twitch itself, as GTA 5 has remained a titan on the platform for years. Users have watched around 9 billion hours of the game and 1.7 billion of those hours came in 2025. Kish kept wanting to stress that this moment is “akin to a moon landing” and compared it to a seismic entertainment moment like a new Star Wars or Lord of the Rings film. As a result, they need to make fans feel that on Twitch.
“It's our responsibility as Twitch to say, ‘How do we show up and give them the best GTA experience known to man?’” said Kish. “How do we make this feel reactive and interactive, not passive? Because that's not what we do here. And how do we make you feel like you can be a part of the biggest thing on the planet?”
Twitch is putting all of its energy and money into supporting this launch. Despite not having any official partnership with Rockstar Games, the streaming platform has created custom GTA 6-themed badges that will display next to users who are present for streams of the game during November. The idea is to give fans something similar to signify they were there for a major moment in entertainment history. The company is also giving out 10,000 copies of the game’s Ultimate Edition to random users throughout the month.
Twitch began making its plans “well over six months ago,” according to Kish. Once it became clear that GTA 6 wouldn’t be delayed again, the team began trying to make whatever preparations that it could.
“The GTA tsunami is going to hit us like a ton of bricks and we have to mentally and physically prepare everybody,” said Kish. “All hands on deck, every chef in the kitchen.”
However, despite all of the hype, there has been a bit of discourse in the last week or two before launch. Twitch streamers like Ludwig Ahgren have noted that regardless of how great the game is, its moment might be a blip given it's a single-player game at launch. He suggested that this means that the amount of fun someone could have streaming the game may only last a week or two, but also suggested that viewership might drop because fans will want to experience the game themselves.
Many of the people I spoke to pushed back on this, though. They think this is an opportunity for creators to separate themselves and show their creativity.
“I think you're going to see what certain content creators are made of,” said TGG when speaking with IGN. “I still make some content on GTA 5 single player. I know other creators still make daily [or] weekly content on GTA 5 single player [which is] 13 years old, and GTA 6 is going to be a crazy step above that. I think Rockstar is trying to slow people down. I think Rockstar is trying to get people to live in this world instead of rushing through the story. I think the content creators that lean into that will see far more success than the content creators that don't. The content creators that treat this like a game, a single player story game will be the ones that go to the bottom. The content creators that treat this like a world will probably rise to the top.”
“I think for most streamers, it's probably going to be like we're going to marathon the game, play it, and then that's probably it for most of them,” said Forrest Waldron AKA KreekCraft on Twitch and YouTube. “But I feel like there's a lot you can do, and maybe this is my YouTuber brain talking, but you've got Easter eggs, you've got challenges, you've got speed runs. There's a lot you can do, and especially in a game like this, there's a lot of different things, especially I want to do a fat Jason, fat Lucia play through where you don't exercise them at all and you just make them as big [as possible]. How does that affect the game? So there's a lot of content there.”
Of course, a game like this also means there are a lot of people hoping this will be their big break. Twitch is aware that this an opportunity for smaller names to break out. The platform has made it so anyone can earn money starting from their first stream, if that’s their prerogative. Kish says that Twitch is doing whatever it can to help streamers have the opportunity to succeed.
“I think that there will be people who will make a name for themselves, as there always is every time a major game releases,” said Kish. “I think about times in our history where a game has risen to stardom and then streamers have ridden those coattails not just because the game is good but because that streamer is freaking good and that game propelled them into stardom.
“GTA is going to be a golden ticket for [many] content creators. This is going to propel hundreds if not thousands of content creators to stardom that you have not heard before. There will be names that we will be talking about at Christmas that we do not know today because of GTA. It's going to shake out and we're going to be like panning for creator gold over the next 30 days.”
New creators aren’t the only people trying to achieve something with GTA 6 either. A bunch of extremely popular and established creators who focus on other games and niches are attempting to pivot to GTA with this release. KreekCraft is a Roblox creator with over 17 million subscribers. Up until this summer, he hadn’t really made any content around GTA. He had played the online modes in 4 and 5, but didn’t delve too deep into the story modes. Ultimately, he’s ready to shake things up beyond Roblox and is eager to take a crack at GTA 6.
“As a content creator, I want to do more than just Roblox,” said KreekCraft. “I want to expand out of that. And this is a good opportunity to do that. [...] Part of me is like, I'm so tired of Roblox. I love everybody there, but geez, the decisions they make, it feels like 2012 Activision Blizzard all over again. I don't want to go through this again.
“And then the games, I'm 29 and we're still getting an egg where you run forward and run back, run forward. And it's like, guys, I just can't stream this anymore. And thankfully I'm in a position where I don't have to anymore. And it's like, this is the year I'm going to start prioritizing my mental health and it comes in the shape of this.
The same goes for YouTuber Tyler Smith, AKA tdawgsmitty, who almost exclusively focuses on Call of Duty. However, he has grown tired of the franchise’s annualized antics and has decided that GTA 6 may be an opportunity to find something that makes him a bit happier.
“Today, I sat down and brainstormed for four hours for [GTA 6 video] ideas, and it's like, whoa, I haven't done this in two, three years now because Call of Duty people just want the same thing over and over again,” said Smith.
It’s easy to be cynical and say these guys are just jumping on a bandwagon, but they have legitimate visions for GTA 6 that stretch beyond the first week of hype. It does seem like this is a game where they can break free of tired cycles and flex their creative muscles more. YouTuber Trevor Martin, best known as TmarTn, knows this well.
He also got his start as a Call of Duty YouTuber, with his main channel being dedicated to the shooter franchise. That channel has 3.2 million subscribers… but he hasn’t touched it in seven years. His last video over there was a review of 2019’s Modern Warfare, and then… nothing since then.
He pivoted to his second channel that had been mostly let’s play oriented for the better part of a decade. Although he still plays other games, Martin has also become a respected source for aggregating GTA 6 news in the last few years. He estimates that he’s uploaded between 800 - 900 GTA 5 videos, which have accumulated over 200 million views collectively. The decision to move away from Call of Duty wasn’t an intentional one, though.
“Honestly, it wasn't like a decision that I made,” said Martin. “When I uploaded that video, I had no idea I wouldn't upload to that channel again. I think I was really lucky in that sense that it was just super natural and it was just wherever my interests were taking me. Luckily, I had built an audience that loved the let's plays and the walkthroughs and things on the other channels. When COD stopped being fun, I just switched my focus.”
He noted that GTA 6 is a great opportunity for people to break out, whether they be new creators or established ones looking for a new direction. He noted this moment is similar to Fortnite’s release, in that it unexpectedly changed the content creation scene, but this time… everyone is expecting it.
“Obviously everyone knows [GTA 6 is releasing], so everyone's going to be grinding. But if you can stand out, I think it's a huge way to break into the space. I also think it's a great way for established creators to reinvent themselves. There's going to be so much, but at the same time, there's so much in the game to make content on that I feel like you can break the mold and you can do unique things and all it takes is one good idea and you can kind of run with it.”
With everyone wanting to get a slice of the GTA pie, there has been a noticeable uptick in AI-generated videos about the game in the run up to release. There are entire creators who believe this game is their golden ticket, but some of them are going to be letting AI do all of the work for them. Some of these videos have generated hundreds of thousands or even millions of views, despite not being made by humans. TGG was quick to note that a lot of these AI channels blatantly copy his and other creators’ videos.
Martin called it “scary” after seeing how easy it was for someone to easily generate a lengthy video with high-quality assets that he would’ve previously needed a budget and a team to produce.
“Those videos, they're pretty well done and they're everywhere and the speed that people can get those out,” he said. “When I watch it, I'm put off by it, but I don't know if other people, especially younger people, are. Because they look great. If you had effects like that back in the day, I remember I used to have effects on [some of my Call of Duty videos], but I had to pay a lot of money for somebody to custom make all these things in [Adobe] After Effects and really highly produce the video. And now it's just a short script away and you can have assets like that.
On one hand, I think it's kind of cool and the technology is amazing. On the other hand, I feel like it kind of loses the love a little bit. You know what I mean? It dehumanizes it. So as tempting as it is, I'm staying super far away from that. I'll stick with simple text PNGs. I don't think videos need that. I think they look nice, but I don't know. I'm really torn on it because I think it's cool, but it's also really concerning.”
Martin went on to note that these types of AI-generated videos excel in informational content. They can rip guides, articles, or summaries from across the internet and spit them out into a new video. As a result, he expects these channels to thrive in the short term with content that teaches players how to make money quickly or unlock certain items. But when it comes to long term success and players looking for more entertaining and original videos? Martin thinks they will “struggle” due the dehumanized nature of AI content.
TGG echoed these sentiments too, noting that a lot of these AI channels blatantly copy their videos.
“I would like to be optimistic and say that people will be able to tell who's being authentic and who's really had these experiences in game and is going along that journey with everyone else,” he said. “And I'd like to think they'd be able to tell the difference between those people and the people that are just riding the hype. I might be wrong. I probably am, but I kind of have to be hopeful that that's the case.”
With GTA 6 being a single-player game at launch, everyone is acutely aware this is only the start of this game’s journey. Although Rockstar itself hasn’t officially announced it, everyone assumes there will be an online mode released later, likely in 2027. After all, GTA Online was a cash cow and Rockstar appears to have laid a fruitful foundation for at least another decade of opportunities and experiences.
The core online experience may only be a sliver of what’s to come for GTA 6. One of the biggest things to spawn from GTA 5 wasn’t actually created by Rockstar itself. Modders created an extremely popular roleplay community that gained a ton of attention during the early 2020s, leading to world renowned figures like LeBron James, Travis Scott, and Kevin Durant all playing the game. Rockstar ended up acquiring the team behind FiveM, which created the modding tools that birthed this content.
Fans expect that Rockstar will utilize this team to build out an official GTA 6 roleplay community across PC and consoles, if not an entire modding system that can be used across platforms. Bethesda has been doing this for about a decade now, but Rockstar may have the resources to push this forward in all kinds of new ways.
“I think the future for Rockstar is going to be definitely in the [user generated content] direction,” said TGG. “I think roleplay has been a crazy explosion, and I don't think anyone quite expected how many people just wanted to live in these worlds that Rockstar is creating, literally live in them. But you're at a point now where you've got three different games in one. You've got GTA single player, you've got GTA Online, and then you have GTA roleplay. And I think the future of content creation has to involve all three.”
With all of that said, it’s clear that GTA 6 is not just a highly-anticipated release for 2026. It’s a game that will set the tone for potentially a whole decade or more when it comes to content creation. New internet personalities are bound to be created, new trends will be set, and as TGG said, it’s a whole new world that is meant to be explored and dug into. It’s the start of a new era and one that we can only begin to imagine the possibilities of.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

With GTA 6 being a single-player game at launch, everyone is acutely aware this is only the start of this game’s journey. Although Rockstar itself hasn’t officially announced it, everyone assumes there will be an online mode released later, likely in 2027. After all, GTA Online was a cash cow and Rockstar appears to have laid a fruitful foundation for at least another decade of opportunities and experiences.

The core online experience may only be a sliver of what’s to come for GTA 6. One of the biggest things to spawn from GTA 5 wasn’t actually created by Rockstar itself. Modders created an extremely popular roleplay community that gained a ton of attention during the early 2020s, leading to world renowned figures like LeBron James, Travis Scott, and Kevin Durant all playing the game. Rockstar ended up acquiring the team behind FiveM, which created the modding tools that birthed this content.

Fans expect that Rockstar will utilize this team to build out an official GTA 6 roleplay community across PC and consoles, if not an entire modding system that can be used across platforms. Bethesda has been doing this for about a decade now, but Rockstar may have the resources to push this forward in all kinds of new ways.

“I think the future for Rockstar is going to be definitely in the [user generated content] direction,” said TGG. “I think roleplay has been a crazy explosion, and I don't think anyone quite expected how many people just wanted to live in these worlds that Rockstar is creating, literally live in them. But you're at a point now where you've got three different games in one. You've got GTA single player, you've got GTA Online, and then you have GTA roleplay. And I think the future of content creation has to involve all three.”
